text: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
reflection: The people in Micah's day wanted to know how to please God. Should they bring burnt offerings? Thousands of rams? Rivers of oil? Even their firstborn children? They assumed God wanted bigger and more costly religious gestures. Micah's answer was surprisingly simple: "He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?" Three things. Do justly: treat people fairly and honestly. Love mercy: not just show mercy occasionally, but love it, delight in kindness. Walk humbly with thy God: live in daily, humble dependence on Him. None of these require wealth or status. Anyone can do them. But they touch every part of life: how we work, how we treat people, and how we relate to God. This month we will think about integrity and holy living. Micah's three requirements are a good place to start. Live them today.
question: Which of these three could you live out in an ordinary way today: doing justly, loving mercy, or walking humbly?
prayer: Lord, You have shown me what is good: to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with You. Help me live these out in ordinary ways today. Amen.

text: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
reflection: There is a freedom that comes with honesty. Proverbs describes it this way: "He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known." To walk uprightly means to live with integrity, the same in private as in public. And such a person walks surely, with security and confidence. They do not have to keep track of lies. They do not fear being found out. They can look people in the eye. Their footing is solid. The person who perverts their ways lives differently. They must constantly cover their tracks. They worry about exposure. And Proverbs says they shall be known. Sooner or later, crooked paths are revealed. Secrets have a way of coming to light. Integrity is not always the easy path in the moment. Sometimes honesty costs us. But over the long run, it is the path of security and peace. Where are you tempted to cut corners? Choose the upright path today. Walk surely.
question: Where might the upright path cost you something today, and will you choose it anyway?
prayer: Lord, the one who walks uprightly walks surely. Give me courage to choose honesty today, even where it costs me, and let me enjoy the freedom of a clear conscience. Amen.

text: The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.
reflection: Life is full of decisions, and some are complicated. How do we know which way to go? Proverbs offers a guide: "The integrity of the upright shall guide them." Integrity is not just a quality we have. It is a compass that directs us. When we are committed to honesty and righteousness, many decisions become clearer. We do not have to agonize over whether to lie on a form, take credit for someone else's work, or cut a corner that no one will notice. Integrity has already answered those questions. It rules certain options out before we even consider them. The second half of the verse gives the contrast: "the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them." Crookedness eventually brings ruin. Lies multiply. Compromises lead to bigger compromises. What seemed like a shortcut becomes a trap. Let integrity be your guide today. When a decision comes, ask not only what is easiest or most profitable, but what is upright. Follow that.
question: Which decision today could become clearer if you let integrity guide it?
prayer: Lord, let integrity guide my choices today. Keep me from crooked ways, and make my path clear as I commit myself to honesty before You. Amen.

text: The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.
reflection: Our choices do not affect only us. They ripple into the lives of those who come after us. Proverbs says, "The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him." A parent who lives with integrity leaves a legacy far more valuable than money. Children watch how their parents handle honesty, work, conflict, and faith. They absorb those values. Integrity becomes part of the family inheritance. Many people can trace their faith or character back to a parent or grandparent who lived rightly. They remember a father who kept his word, a mother who told the truth when it was hard, or a grandparent who prayed faithfully. Those lives continue to bless generations. This is also true for those without children of their own. Students, nieces, nephews, younger coworkers, and neighbours all watch how we live. What legacy are you building? Every honest choice today is an investment in someone else's tomorrow. Walk in your integrity.
question: What honest choice today could become a blessing to those who come after you?
prayer: Lord, the just one who walks in integrity leaves a blessing to their children. Help me make honest choices today that bless others for years to come. Amen.

text: He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness, and speaketh the truth in his heart.
reflection: Psalm 15 begins with a question: Lord, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? Who may dwell with God? The answer describes a person of integrity, starting with this: "He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness, and speaketh the truth in his heart." Notice the last phrase: speaketh the truth in his heart. Truth is not only about what we say out loud. It begins inside. It means being honest with ourselves and with God. It means not deceiving ourselves about our motives, our sins, or our needs. Many people speak truthfully to others while telling themselves comfortable lies. I am not that bad. It was not my fault. I can handle this on my own. Honesty in the heart is the foundation of all other honesty. When we are truthful inside, truthfulness flows out in our words and actions. Today, take a few moments to be completely honest with God about your heart. Let truth begin on the inside.
question: Is there anything in your heart you have not been completely honest with God about?
prayer: Lord, I want to speak the truth in my heart. Help me be completely honest with You today, and with myself, about what is really inside me. Amen.

text: He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart; who hath not lifted up his soul unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully.
reflection: Psalm 24 asks who may ascend the hill of the Lord and stand in His holy place. The answer: "He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart; who hath not lifted up his soul unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully." Clean hands refer to our actions. What we do. Pure heart refers to our motives. Why we do it. God cares about both. It is possible to do the right things for the wrong reasons, or to have good intentions while doing wrong things. God desires integrity in both. Not lifting up the soul unto vanity means not giving our devotion to empty things, to idols of any kind. Not swearing deceitfully means keeping our word. No one meets this standard perfectly. That is why we need a Saviour. But through Christ, we are cleansed and given new hearts. And by His Spirit, we grow in holiness. Ask God today to clean your hands and purify your heart. Let both your actions and motives honour Him.
question: Where do your actions or your motives need God's cleansing today?
prayer: Lord, I want clean hands and a pure heart. You care about what I do and why I do it. Cleanse my actions, purify my motives, and keep my words honest. Amen.

text: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
reflection: David wrote Psalm 51 after his terrible sin with Bathsheba was exposed. He had committed adultery and arranged the death of her husband. When the prophet Nathan confronted him, David broke. He did not make excuses. He poured out his heart in confession. And in the middle of the psalm, he prayed, "Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me." The word create is the same word used in Genesis when God created the heavens and the earth. David knew he could not fix his own heart. He needed God to do something new, something only the Creator could do. He did not ask for a cleaned-up version of his old heart. He asked for a new one. Here is hope for anyone who feels their heart is too far gone. God does not just patch us up. He creates new hearts. Pray David's prayer today. Ask God to create something clean and new in you.
question: What in your heart do you need God to make new, not just patch up?
prayer: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. Only You can make my heart new. Do Your creating work in me today. Amen.

text: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts…
reflection: Psalm 139 is a long meditation on how completely God knows us. He knows when we sit and when we rise. He knows our thoughts before we think them. He formed us in the womb. There is nowhere we can go to escape His presence. And at the end of the psalm, David invites God to do what He already does: "Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts." This is a brave prayer. Most of us would rather keep certain parts of our hearts hidden. We prefer not to look too closely at our motives, our anxieties, or our secret sins. But David opens the door. He asks God to search every corner. Why? Because God's searching is not to condemn but to heal. The Great Physician examines us to find what needs treatment. We cannot fix what we will not face. Pray David's prayer slowly today. Invite God to search your heart and know your thoughts.
question: Are you willing to ask God to search your heart today, trusting He searches to heal?
prayer: Search me, O God, and know my heart; try me, and know my thoughts. I open my heart to You, trusting that You search me to heal and not to condemn. Amen.

text: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
reflection: David's prayer continues: "And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting." He asks God to find anything wrong, any wicked way, any path that leads away from God. This is not someone defending himself. It is someone who wants to be corrected. Then David asks for direction: lead me in the way everlasting. Searching is not the end goal. Being led is. God does not expose our faults just to make us feel bad. He reveals them so He can lead us onto a better path. The way everlasting is the path that lasts, the road that leads to life. This two-part prayer is a pattern for spiritual growth. First, let God show you what is wrong. Second, let Him lead you to what is right. Both require humility. Both require trust. If God has been showing you something that needs to change, do not resist. Let Him lead you in the way everlasting.
question: What might God want to change in you today so He can lead you on a better path?
prayer: Lord, see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting. Show me what needs to change, and give me grace to follow where You lead. Amen.

text: Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.
reflection: Psalm 19 begins with the heavens declaring God's glory and moves to the perfection of God's Word. Then it ends with a personal prayer: "Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer." Words of my mouth: what we say. Meditation of my heart: what we think about. Both matter to God. Words often reveal what has been growing in our hearts. If our thoughts are bitter, our words will eventually be bitter too. If our thoughts are filled with God's truth, our words will reflect it. David wanted both to be acceptable in God's sight. Not just in the sight of others. It is possible to say the right things in public while harbouring wrong thoughts in private. Integrity means our inner life and outer words match, and both please God. This verse makes a wonderful prayer to begin any day. Say it before you speak to anyone else today.
question: Before you speak to anyone today, could you pray that your words and thoughts would please God?
prayer: Lord, let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in Your sight, O Lord, my strength and my redeemer. Amen.

text: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
reflection: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus pronounced blessings on unlikely people: the poor in spirit, the mourners, the meek. Then He said, "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God." Purity of heart means single-mindedness. A pure heart is not divided. It does not chase God with one hand and the world with the other. It wants God above all. It is undiluted, sincere, and wholehearted. The religious leaders of Jesus' day focused on outward purity: washing hands, avoiding unclean foods, following rituals. Jesus pointed to the heart. That is where true purity begins. And the reward is wonderful: they shall see God. Not just in eternity, though that is included, but even now. A pure heart perceives God's presence more clearly. When our hearts are cluttered with competing desires, it is hard to see Him. When our hearts are focused, He becomes clearer. Ask God today for a pure heart. Ask Him to remove whatever divides your devotion.
question: What is dividing your heart between God and the world right now?
prayer: Lord, blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God. Remove whatever divides my heart, and give me single-minded devotion to You. Amen.

text: But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
reflection: In Jesus' day, people swore oaths to back up their promises. They swore by heaven, by earth, by Jerusalem, or by their own heads. Some even used clever loopholes, swearing by things that did not technically bind them. Jesus cut through all of it: "But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil." In other words, just say yes or no, and mean it. A person of integrity does not need to swear or add dramatic promises to be believed. Their word is enough. If they say yes, they will do it. If they say no, they mean it. This applies to everyday life. Do we keep our commitments? Do we show up when we said we would? Do we follow through on small promises? Or do people learn not to count on our words? Being reliable is a form of holiness. Today, let your yes be yes. Keep every promise, large and small.
question: Is there a promise, large or small, you need to keep today?
prayer: Lord Jesus, let my yes be yes and my no be no. Make me reliable in my word, and help me keep every promise I make today. Amen.

text: But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation…
reflection: Peter wrote to scattered believers living among people who did not share their faith. He urged them to live distinctively: "But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation." In the King James Version, conversation means conduct, the whole way we live. Not just our words, but our behaviour, habits, and choices. Holiness is not only for church or prayer time. It reaches into every part of life: how we work, how we spend money, what we watch, how we drive, how we treat people who cannot benefit us. The reason is simple. The One who called us is holy. Children tend to resemble their parents. As God's children, we are called to reflect His character. Holiness is not about being odd or self-righteous. It is about being set apart for God, living in a way that shows we belong to Him. Think of one area of your life you have kept separate from God. Invite His holiness in today.
question: What area of your life have you kept separate from God that you could invite His holiness into?
prayer: Lord, You who called me are holy. Make me holy in all my conduct, not just in some moments. I invite You into the part of my life I have kept apart from You. Amen.

text: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
reflection: After eleven chapters explaining the mercies of God, Paul turns to how we should respond: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service." The word therefore points back to everything God has done. Because of His mercy, our response is to give ourselves completely to Him. In the Old Testament, sacrifices were killed and placed on the altar. Paul calls for a living sacrifice. Not a one-time offering, but a daily surrender of our whole selves. Our bodies, which include our actions, words, time, and energy, are offered to God. The problem with a living sacrifice, someone has said, is that it keeps crawling off the altar. That is why it must be renewed daily. Paul calls this reasonable service, the logical response to God's mercy. When we understand how much He has given us, offering ourselves back is the only thing that makes sense. Present yourself to Him today.
question: What would it look like to offer yourself to God again today as a living sacrifice?
prayer: Lord, in view of all Your mercies, I present myself to You as a living sacrifice. Take all of me again today, for this is my reasonable service. Amen.

text: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
reflection: Right after calling us to be living sacrifices, Paul explains how that works: "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind." Conformed means pressed into a mould. The world constantly pushes us to think like it, value what it values, and live as it lives. Without realizing it, we can be shaped by its ideas about success, beauty, pleasure, and identity. Paul says resist the mould. Instead, be transformed. The word is metamorphosis, the same word used for a caterpillar becoming a butterfly. Real change from the inside out. And it happens through the renewing of your mind. As we fill our minds with God's truth, our thinking changes. As our thinking changes, our lives change. The result is that we can prove, or discover by experience, what God's will is: good, acceptable, and perfect. What is shaping your mind these days? Feed it with God's Word today. Let Him transform you from the inside out.
question: Where is the world pressing you into its mould, and how could God's Word renew your mind there?
prayer: Lord, keep me from being conformed to this world. Transform me by the renewing of my mind, and fill my thinking with Your truth today. Amen.

text: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
reflection: What we think about shapes who we become. Paul knew this, so he gave the Philippians a filter for their thoughts: "whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things." Eight qualities. True, not false. Honest, worthy of respect. Just, right and fair. Pure, clean and wholesome. Lovely, beautiful and pleasing. Of good report, admirable. Virtuous. Praiseworthy. This is not about ignoring problems or pretending everything is fine. It is about choosing what we dwell on. Our minds will fill with something. If we do not choose good things, other things will rush in: worry, bitterness, envy, impurity. Today, run your thoughts through Paul's filter. When something does not pass, replace it. Think on these things, and watch your heart follow.
question: Which of your thoughts today needs to pass through Paul's filter of what is true, pure, and lovely?
prayer: Lord, help me think on whatever is true, honest, just, pure, lovely, and of good report. Guard my thoughts today, and shape my character through them. Amen.

text: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
reflection: Daniel was a young man taken captive to Babylon. He was chosen to be trained in the king's court, given a new name, and offered food from the king's own table. Much of it would have violated God's law or been offered to idols. It would have been easy to go along. He was far from home, in a powerful empire, with his future in the king's hands. But "Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself." He made a decision before the pressure peaked. He settled it in his heart. And then he acted wisely. He did not rebel or make a scene. He respectfully asked for an alternative, a ten-day test of vegetables and water. God gave him favour, and the test succeeded. Integrity often begins with a decision made in advance. When we decide beforehand what we will and will not do, we are much stronger when temptation comes. What do you need to purpose in your heart today?
question: What could you settle in your heart today before temptation comes?
prayer: Lord, Daniel purposed in his heart not to defile himself. Help me decide ahead of time what I will and will not do, and give me wisdom and grace to stand. Amen.

text: There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
reflection: Joseph was a slave in Egypt, serving in the house of Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh. He worked so faithfully that Potiphar put him in charge of everything. Then Potiphar's wife began to pressure Joseph day after day to sleep with her. Joseph refused: "There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?" Joseph saw the situation clearly. It would betray his master's trust. But more than that, it would be sin against God. That was the deciding factor. He was far from his family, and no one in Egypt would likely have known. But God would know. Joseph's integrity cost him dearly. He was falsely accused and thrown into prison. But God was with him there too. Integrity may cost us in the short term. But it honours God, and He does not forget. Stand firm today.
question: Where are you tempted today, and how does remembering that sin is against God help you stand?
prayer: Lord, how can I do this great wickedness and sin against You? When temptation comes today, help me stand firm as Joseph did, and be with me as You were with him. Amen.

text: God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.
reflection: Job's friends insisted that his suffering must be punishment for hidden sin. If he would just confess, they said, God would restore him. Job could have given in. He could have admitted to wrongs he did not commit just to end the argument. But he refused: "God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me." Job would not lie, even to make his situation easier. He would not agree with something false, even under pressure from people he respected. His integrity was more important than his comfort or reputation. This takes great courage. Sometimes the pressure to compromise comes from those close to us. Friends, family, or coworkers may urge us to say what is not true, to go along with something wrong, or to take blame we do not deserve. Integrity means holding fast to the truth even then. Hold on to your integrity today. It is worth more than temporary relief.
question: Is anyone pressuring you to compromise the truth, and how could you hold fast to it today?
prayer: Lord, like Job, I will hold fast my integrity and not let it go. When others press me to compromise, give me courage to hold on to what is true. Amen.

text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
reflection: As Job defended his integrity, he described the standards he had set for himself. One of them was this: "I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?" Job understood that purity begins with the eyes. What we look at feeds what we think about. And what we think about shapes what we do. So he made a covenant, a solemn agreement, with his eyes. He decided ahead of time not to look at women with lust. This is ancient wisdom that speaks powerfully today. We are surrounded by images on screens, billboards, and phones. Many of them are designed to capture our attention and stir our desires. Without a deliberate decision, our eyes will wander. Job shows that purity is not passive. It requires a commitment and boundaries. It is not about shame but about protecting the heart. What covenant might you need to make with your eyes? Set boundaries today that guard your heart and honour God.
question: What boundaries do you need to set with your eyes today?
prayer: Lord, help me make a covenant with my eyes. Guard what I choose to look at, keep my heart pure, and give me strength to turn away from what dishonours You. Amen.

text: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
reflection: If you had to protect one thing above all else, what would it be? Proverbs gives an answer: "Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life." The heart in Scripture is not just the seat of emotions. It is the centre of the whole person: thoughts, desires, will, and choices. And Proverbs says everything in life flows from it. Like a spring that feeds a river, the heart determines the quality of everything downstream. A polluted spring produces polluted water. A clean spring produces clean water. That is why we must keep, or guard, our hearts with all diligence. This means paying attention to what we let in: what we watch, read, listen to, and dwell on. It means noticing bitterness, envy, or lust before they take root. It means filling our hearts with God's Word and presence. Guarding the heart is not a one-time task but a daily practice. Guard your heart today with care.
question: What have you been allowing into your heart that you need to guard against?
prayer: Lord, help me keep my heart with all diligence, for out of it are the issues of life. Show me what I am letting in, and help me guard my heart well today. Amen.

text: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
reflection: Many people spend their lives chasing wealth. Proverbs suggests a better pursuit: "A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold." A good name means a good reputation, built on trustworthy character. It is what people think of when they hear your name. And Proverbs says it is worth more than great riches. Why? Money can be lost in a moment. It can buy many things, but not trust or respect. A good name is built slowly through years of honest choices, and it opens doors that money cannot. People trust you. They seek your counsel. They speak well of you even when you are not present. Loving favour, being held in warm regard by others, is worth more than silver and gold. Of course, a good name should not be our ultimate goal; pleasing God is. But a life lived for God naturally builds a good name. Choose character over cash today.
question: Where could you choose good character over gain today?
prayer: Lord, a good name is rather to be chosen than great riches. Help me value trustworthy character above money, and choose what is right today. Amen.

text: Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight.
reflection: Few verses are as direct as this one: "Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight." Abomination is a strong word. It means something God finds deeply offensive. Lying is not a small matter to Him. God is truth itself, and lies contradict His nature. But the second half of the verse is just as strong, in a positive direction. Those who deal truly are His delight. God takes pleasure in honest people. When we tell the truth, especially when it is hard, we bring Him joy. Lying can creep in subtly. Exaggerating a story. Making excuses. Telling people what they want to hear. Shading the facts to look better. These may seem harmless, but they chip away at integrity. Dealing truly means being honest in word and in action. It means keeping our dealings fair and our words reliable. Today, make it your aim to be someone God delights in. Deal truly in everything.
question: Where could you be more careful to deal truly in your words and actions today?
prayer: Lord, lying lips are an abomination to You, but those who deal truly are Your delight. Make me honest in every word and every action today. Amen.

text: Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.
reflection: Paul gives a practical instruction in Ephesians 4: "Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another." The reason he gives is interesting. Not just that lying is wrong, though it is. But because we are members one of another. We are connected, like parts of a body. Imagine if your eyes lied to your hands about where an object was. Or if your nerves sent false signals to your brain. The body would not function. It would hurt itself. In the same way, when believers lie to each other, the whole body suffers. Trust breaks down. Relationships are damaged. Unity is lost. Truth-telling is not just a personal virtue. It is essential for community. Healthy families, friendships, churches, and workplaces all depend on honest communication. Today, put away any form of lying. Speak truth to those around you, with love and grace. You are connected, and truth keeps the body healthy.
question: Is there someone you need to speak the truth to in love today?
prayer: Lord, help me put away lying and speak truth with those around me, for we are members one of another. Let my truth always be spoken in love. Amen.

text: Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.
reflection: Words are powerful. They can wound or heal, tear down or build up. Paul gives a clear guideline: "Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers." Corrupt here means rotten, like spoiled fruit. Rotten words include gossip, crude jokes, cutting sarcasm, and harsh criticism. Paul says none of it should come out of our mouths. Instead, our words should be good for edifying, building others up. And they should minister grace to those who hear them. Imagine if every conversation left people encouraged rather than discouraged. Imagine if your words were a gift of grace to everyone who heard them. That is the goal. This does not mean we never say anything hard. Sometimes truth needs to be spoken. But even hard truths can be spoken in a way that builds up. Today, before you speak, ask: will this build up? Will it give grace?
question: Before you speak today, how could you make sure your words will build someone up?
prayer: Lord, let no corrupt communication come out of my mouth. Let my words build others up and give grace to those who hear them today. Amen.

text: And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men…
reflection: Paul wrote this instruction to servants, people who often worked hard for masters who did not appreciate them: "And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men." Heartily means from the soul, with full effort and sincerity. And the key is who we are really working for. Not just for a boss, a teacher, or a client. For the Lord. This changes everything about work. A boring task becomes an offering. An unappreciated job becomes worship. Doing our best even when no one is watching becomes a way of honouring God. It also frees us from the need for human approval. If we work only for people's praise, we will be disappointed. People often fail to notice. But God always sees. The next verse promises that we will receive the reward of the inheritance from the Lord. Whatever work is before you today, at home, in an office, in a classroom, or anywhere else, do it heartily. Do it for Him.
question: Which task today could you do heartily, as for the Lord and not for people?
prayer: Lord, whatever I do today, help me do it heartily, as to You and not to people. Turn my work into worship, and free me from needing others' approval. Amen.

text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
reflection: Jesus taught that character is revealed in small things: "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much." We often think big moments define us. But Jesus says the little things matter just as much. How we handle small amounts of money. Whether we keep minor promises. How we act when we think no one is looking. Whether we are honest about small details. These reveal who we really are. Someone who cheats on small things will likely cheat on big ones. Someone who is faithful in little will be faithful in much. Integrity is not built in grand gestures. It is built in a thousand small choices. Returning extra change. Admitting a small mistake. Finishing a task properly. Showing up on time. These may seem insignificant, but they shape our character. Today, pay attention to the little things. Be faithful in what is least.
question: What small, everyday choice today could be a test of your faithfulness?
prayer: Lord Jesus, the one who is faithful in the least is faithful also in much. Help me be faithful in the little things today, where integrity is built. Amen.

text: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
reflection: Timothy was a young leader, and some older believers may have doubted him because of his age. Paul encouraged him: "Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity." Paul did not tell Timothy to argue for his authority. He told him to earn respect through his example. Six areas are named. Word: what he says. Conversation: how he lives. Charity: how he loves. Spirit: his attitude. Faith: his trust in God. Purity: his moral life. These are areas where anyone, at any age, can set an example. You do not need a title or position to influence others. You need consistent, godly character. This verse speaks especially to young people. You do not have to wait until you are older to make a difference. You can be an example now. And it speaks to everyone. In which of these six areas could you be a better example today?
question: In which area could you set a godly example today: word, conduct, love, spirit, faith, or purity?
prayer: Lord, help me be an example in word, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity. Let my character speak louder than my age or title. Amen.

text: Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
reflection: Paul gave Timothy a two-part strategy for holy living: "Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart." Flee and follow. Some temptations should not be fought or reasoned with. They should be fled from. Joseph ran from Potiphar's wife. That was not weakness; it was wisdom. Some battles are best won by not being there at all. But fleeing is only half the strategy. If we only run from wrong without running toward right, we leave an empty space. So Paul says follow, or pursue, righteousness, faith, love, and peace. Fill the space with good things. And notice the last phrase: with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. We are not meant to do this alone. Godly friends make it easier to flee temptation and pursue righteousness. What do you need to flee from today? And what do you need to pursue? Find companions who will help you.
question: What do you need to flee from today, and what do you need to pursue?
prayer: Lord, help me flee what draws me from You and follow righteousness, faith, love, and peace. Surround me with companions who call on You from a pure heart. Amen.

text: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.
reflection: John wrote about the difference between walking in darkness and walking in light. Then he gave this promise: "But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin." Walking in the light means living openly and honestly before God, not hiding anything from Him. It does not mean being perfect. John says in the next verses that if we claim to have no sin, we deceive ourselves. Walking in the light means bringing our sins into the open, confessing them, and receiving cleansing. Two results follow. First, fellowship with one another. When we are honest with God, we can be honest with others. Real relationships grow. Second, cleansing from all sin. Not some, but all. The blood of Jesus is enough for every failure. Today, step into the light. Hide nothing from God. Receive His cleansing and enjoy real fellowship.
question: Is there anything you are hiding from God that you could bring into the light today?
prayer: Lord, I want to walk in the light as You are in the light. I hide nothing from You today. Thank You that the blood of Jesus cleanses me from all sin. Amen.

text: I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way. O when wilt thou come unto me? I will walk within my house with a perfect heart.
reflection: Psalm 101 is a king's pledge of how he will rule. David begins with his own life before mentioning anyone else: "I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way. O when wilt thou come unto me? I will walk within my house with a perfect heart." Notice where David starts: within my house. Before he addresses how he will govern a nation, he commits to integrity at home. Home is where integrity is most tested. In public, we can put on a good face. At home, people see who we really are. Our families know our moods, our habits, and our hidden attitudes. A perfect heart here means a wholehearted, sincere heart, not a flawless one. It is a heart undivided in its commitment to God. This month we have thought about integrity and holy living. End it where David began: at home. How can you walk with a sincere heart within your own house today? Let your integrity start there.
question: Where is integrity most tested for you at home, and what commitment could you make there?
prayer: Lord, help me walk within my house with a perfect heart. Let my integrity be real at home first, where it matters most and is tested most. Amen.
